project.title: Simple Pendulum — Time in Motion
project.audience: Grades 8–11 continuum: intuitive exploration first, with optional quantitative practical work for learners comfortable with periods, units and graphs.
project.outcome: Measure full-cycle periods, compare controlled trials, and estimate gravitational acceleration from a T²–L graph while explaining the small-angle assumption and one real-lab source of uncertainty.
project.session: A 10–20 minute core investigation, with optional extended practical work.
project.devices: Desktop and tablet browsers; keyboard and single-pointer alternatives to direct dragging.
project.delivery: Bundled static React/TypeScript/Three.js application, published with Sites; relative-path production output also suitable for a future GitHub Pages subpath.

identity.composition: Deep-blue cinematic opening and instrument stage, brass pendulum, clear light laboratory controls, linked energy trace and experimental notebook.
identity.interaction: Drag and release the bob, isolate one parameter, slow the same physical motion, time repeated centre crossings, record and compare.
identity.signature: A shared physical state ties visible bob motion to angle, energy and actual crossing-time measurements; notebook trials can restore their conditions and contribute eligible points to a gravity fit.
identity.distinction: Trajectory and time are the dominant interactions; a dark kinetic stage, live graph composition and experiment notebook distinguish this from the earlier ivory metrology instrument galleries.

model.scope: Nonlinear planar simple pendulum with optional linear angular-velocity damping; the undamped small-angle equation is a labelled comparison, not the integration model.
model.units: SI: length in metres, time in simulated seconds, gravity in m/s², mass in kg, damping rate γ in s⁻¹, energy in J. Angles are radians internally and degrees at the release control.
model.state: Authoritative θ, ω, simulated time and independently integrated dissipated energy Q. Parameters are length, gravity, mass, damping and release angle. Recorded trials and prediction-card selections are separate from live physical state.
model.equation: θ̇ = ω; ω̇ = −(g/L)sinθ − γω; Q̇ = γmL²ω².
model.integration: Classical RK4 at fixed dt = 1/240 s, independent of display refresh and playback rate; graph samples every 1/30 simulated second, retained in a bounded buffer.
model.observation: Period comes from successive positive-going centre crossings with linear within-step event interpolation. The first crossing arms timing; a subsequent crossing completes a full period.
model.domain: L 0.25–2.5 m; g 0.5–25 m/s²; mass 0.1–2 kg; γ 0–1 s⁻¹; release −80° to +80°. Zero motion and overdamped states do not imply an observed oscillation period.
assumptions: Point mass at the visible bob centre; length is measured from pivot to centre.
Massless inextensible suspension, fixed pivot, uniform gravity and one vertical plane.
Linear resistance is normalized as angular damping rate γ; it is not a calibrated air-density setting.
Potential energy is zero at the lowest position; K + U + Q is the energy account for an unchanged free run.
limitations: No suspension stretch or mass, finite-bob rotational inertia, moving support, forcing, quadratic drag, dry friction, out-of-plane motion or Earth-rotation effect.
Theoretical finite-amplitude periods are undamped references. The small-angle gravity inference retains finite-amplitude bias even for otherwise perfect simulated measurements.
The notebook adds no fabricated reaction-time noise; a real practical includes handling and measurement uncertainty.
Graphics, browser offline lifecycle, accessibility and classroom outcomes require their own evidence; numerical results alone do not certify them.

invariants.statement: At fixed γ, changing mass alone leaves angular motion unchanged while energies scale with mass.
invariants.oracle: Independent mass-scaled runs and dimensional energy comparison in tests/physics.test.ts.

invariants.statement: Undamped mechanical energy is conserved within the declared numerical bound; damping reduces mechanical energy while independently integrated Q preserves the balance.
invariants.oracle: Fastest allowed 80° run: relative undamped drift below 2e-6 over 120 simulated seconds; damped balance error below 2e-7 over the tested interval.

invariants.statement: Observed periods are full-cycle, same-direction crossing intervals and agree with independently evaluated limiting/reference cases.
invariants.oracle: Analytic tiny-angle period, independent Simpson quadrature for finite-amplitude periods, explicit half-cycle and duplicate-sample cases.

invariants.statement: Physical length and angle in the rendered apparatus agree with pivot-to-centre model geometry.
invariants.oracle: Rendered datum inspection at minimum/maximum lengths and signed release angles, with 3D and fallback evidence kept separate.

build.note: Partial verification record, not full release certification. Retain blocked/unverified capability gates; refresh final build and artifact bindings after any relevant changes.

requirements.description: Scientifically accurate nonlinear model, energy and period references.
requirements.acceptance: Domain validation, analytic limits, independent finite-amplitude references, energy balance and convergence checks pass with stated bounds; unsupported states have explicit behavior.

requirements.description: A draggable bob and equivalent non-drag operation.
requirements.acceptance: Pointer drag/release, cancellation and a labelled angle-control route set the same bounded physical release without fighting page scrolling or changing length.

requirements.description: Working length, gravity, damping and playback controls with honest time.
requirements.acceptance: Physical changes restart dependent traces/timing; pause, step and slow motion preserve a consistent simulated clock; background interruption cannot create a large time jump.

requirements.description: Live energy and angle graphs derived from model samples.
requirements.acceptance: The current visible graph, numeric values and bob state agree; axes and SI units are correct; paths use sampled data without misleading smoothing or a wall-time scale.

requirements.description: Period measurement, observation notebook and T²–L gravity inference.
requirements.acceptance: Measure, record, replay and export a complete trial; obtain a fit from at least three distinct eligible lengths under the same gravity, zero damping and small release conditions; flag excluded rows.

requirements.description: Distinct, legible 3D visuals and accessible essential tasks.
requirements.acceptance: Inspect actual WebGL opening and active lab views, minimum/maximum apparatus states and narrow layouts; essential keyboard/non-drag paths, focus, labels and reduced-motion behavior work without blocked controls.
A clean packaged production entry and assets work at the intended base/subpath and the published Site reports successful deployment; source and operational instructions match the build.

requirements.description: Coherent local offline release and safe updates.
requirements.acceptance: Complete cache preparation, a network-disabled reload/restart, optional feature use, update preservation and incomplete-cache handling are observed; readiness is never inferred from manifest existence alone.

requirements.description: Local observation persistence with explicit failure and reset semantics.
requirements.acceptance: Saved observations survive reload; corrupt/unavailable storage has useful feedback; restart preserves trials and notebook clear can be undone; exported values match stored observations.

Each prediction card accepts a choice, distinguishes a correct and incorrect explanation, and supports retry; feedback remains readable and accessible without claiming secure assessment or measured learning impact.

checks.method: Executed 21 Vitest domain tests plus deterministic energy/period probes; independent analytic and quadrature references, convergence, domain rejection and event-direction checks. Source/test hashes in the artifact match the current files.
checks.environment: Managed Linux workspace; Node 24.22.1; Vitest 3.2.4; 14 November 2026. This is a domain-only check, not rendered/browser validation.
